lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eS = k ln W\u003c/b\u0: "S = k ln W: entropy measures microstates."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl fundir y, sobre to:
"

On melting and, above all, on vaporizing, the particles gain freedom: for water, S° = 41 J/(mol·K) (ice, approximate value) → 69.9 (liquid) → 188.8 (vapor). More atoms per molecule, greater mass and higher T also increase S. Reactions that produce gas or increase the number of moles have ΔS > 0.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl quitar la partició:
"

When the partition is removed, the particles spread throughout the container. For the isothermal expansion of an ideal gas from V to 2V: ΔS = nR ln 2 = +5.76 J/(mol·K). The process is spontaneous with no change in energy: it is driven by entropy alone. The second law: ΔSuniverse > 0 in every spontaneous process.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eBoltzmann definió \u0:
"

Boltzmann defined S = kB ln W, with kB = 1.38×10⁻²³ J/K. For one mole, S = R ln(W) per particle. More microstates means greater entropy. An isolated system evolves toward the macrostate with the greatest W, simply because it is the most probable: the 50/50 distribution.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eComo ΔS\u003csub\u003:
"

Since ΔSsurr = −ΔH/T, the criterion ΔSuniv > 0 is equivalent to ΔG = ΔH − TΔS < 0 (at constant P and T). There are four cases according to the signs: (−,+) always spontaneous; (+,−) never; (−,−) spontaneous at low T; (+,+) spontaneous at high T. The crossover temperature is T = ΔH/ΔS.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon \u003cb\u003eN pa:
"

With N particles distributed between two halves, each specific assignment of every particle is a microstate; the macrostate only says how many are on the left (k). The number of microstates is W = N!/(k!(N−k)!). With 20 particles there is a single microstate with all on the left, but 184,756 with 10 and 10.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el equilibrio ΔG =:
"

At equilibrium ΔG = 0 and ΔG° = −RT ln K. If ΔG° < 0, K > 1 (favors products); if ΔG° > 0, K < 1. Every 5.7 kJ/mol at 298 K changes K by a factor of 10. Change T and the reaction in “Lab” and watch how K moves with temperature.

"
